name: fdatasync
description: fdatasync() synchronizes a file's in-core data with the storage device, similar to fsync(), but only flushes data and necessary metadata. This reduces disk activity for applications that do not require all metadata to be synchronized with the disk.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the file to synchronize.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: fd is not a valid open file descriptor.
The function was interrupted by a signal.
Disk space was exhausted while synchronizing.
fd is bound to a special file which does not support synchronization.
fd is bound to a file on NFS or another filesystem where a previous write failed due to insufficient storage space.

bugs: In Linux 2.2 and earlier, fdatasync() is equivalent to fsync(), offering no performance advantage. Older kernels and some filesystems may not properly flush disk caches.
versions: Available since POSIX.1-2001; in Linux, equivalent to fsync() in versions 2.2 and earlier.
